subject: Post-demo: unit-cost breakdown & test plan to validate hyperscaler gap
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: unit-cost breakdown & test plan to validate hyperscaler gap

Samir — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and a concrete test plan so we can validate the cost delta you saw against the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned.

Recap / measured unit economics (approx):
- Hyperscaler (your current managed endpoint): quoted ~$95–120 per 1M tokens for the model class you demoed (their variable pricing + egress).
- Redwood (hosted, with default batching): baseline measured ~ $75 per 1M tokens for the same model (4-bit quantized variant) over sample workload. This assumes ~60% KV cache hit and average request length of ~64 tokens.
- Optimized projection: with persistent prefix caching improvements and larger batching, we can reach ~$40–50 per 1M tokens at ~80% cache hit / steady-state.

Key differentiators that matter for TCO:
- Cache-hit leverage: our KV prefix caching reduces repeated generation cost for chat-style workloads.
- Workload-aware batching: better throughput without linear latency increase for majority of requests.
- Fallback routing: automatic swap to cheaper quantized variant when SLOs allow it (keeps 99th percentile latency and reduces token cost).

Proposed validation tests (attached workbook has scenario matrix):
1) Synthetic 1M-token run (single model): run three experiments varying batch sizes {1, 8, 32} and record p50/p95 latency, GPU util, and per-token cost.
2) Cache-hit sweep: run same workload with KV cache hit rates {20%, 50%, 80%} to show marginal benefit and identify the inflection point.
3) Mixed requests: 70/30 short/long prompt mix to capture real traffic distribution.
4) Hyperscaler side-by-side: you send us a locked-down test token/endpoint (if allowed) or we side-by-side using the same input corpus — measure token costs and latency under same batch profile.

Attachments included: HR-1M-token-scenarios.xlsx (workload matrix), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-config-diff.txt (how we’ll align runtimes), mutual-action-plan-HR.pdf (MMP with milestones).

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm whether HyperRun can provision a temporary read-only endpoint or we should run an indistinguishable input replay?
- Do you have a preferred 2–3 hour window next week for benchmarking (we recommend off-peak hours to avoid noisy neighbors)?
- Can you share a representative 10K prompt sample so we can pre-warm KV-cache assumptions?

I’ve cc’d Ben to own the benchmarking harness; he’ll propose owners/timestamps. If this sounds good I can spin up the test configs and share a live dashboard for results.

— Kimberly Park

- Our hyperscaler invoices for comparable endpoint usage land around $95 per 1M tokens (agreed on the range in your note).
